title: Assemble a flat-pack bookcase
safety: A tall bookcase can tip over. Anchor it to the wall before you load it.
Lift heavy boxes and the finished bookcase with a second person.
Keep small fittings away from children and pets.

steps.say: Clear a space and lay down a blanket or the flattened box.
steps.detail: Build it in the room where it will stay, so you do not have to carry it through doorways. The soft surface protects the floor and the panels.

steps.say: Open the box without cutting into the panels.
steps.detail: If you need a blade, cut only the tape and keep it shallow, so you do not scratch the finish.

steps.say: Find the manual and check every part against its parts list.
steps.detail: Count each panel, screw, dowel and cam lock before you start. Say I'm missing, then the part, and I'll find where to get it.

steps.say: Sort the small fittings into bowls.
steps.detail: Keep one type in each bowl. Screws and cam locks are easy to lose and easy to mix up.

steps.say: Follow the manual's frame steps, tightening screws by hand only.
steps.detail: Fit the dowels and cam locks in the order the manual shows. Leaving everything slightly loose makes it easier to line the panels up.

steps.say: Check the frame is square, then tighten everything firmly.
steps.detail: Tighten until snug and stop there. Too much force can strip the screw hole or crack the board.

steps.say: Fit the back panel the way the manual shows.
steps.detail: The back panel keeps the bookcase rigid, so do not skip it. Fix it along all the edges the manual marks.

steps.say: Stand it up with a helper and anchor it to the wall.
steps.detail: Use fixings that suit your wall type. Do not load the shelves until it is anchored.
